claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered single-phase BCC solid solution.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of approximately 1719 MPa.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has limited room-temperature compressive plasticity.
Partially replacing Mo with additional Nb will lower the alloy's overall electronegativity difference.
A lower overall electronegativity difference will modify local bonding characteristics and reduce disparities in bonding strength among the constituent elements.
Reduced disparity in local bonding strengths will facilitate dislocation motion.
Facilitated dislocation motion will enhance room-temperature compressive plasticity.
Partial substitution of Mo with Nb will produce approximately a 20% relative increase in ductility.
The Nb-substituted alloy will retain at least approximately 80% of the baseline compressive yield strength.
The retained compressive yield strength will be at least approximately 1375 MPa.
The proposed effect is limited to compositions and processing conditions that preserve a single-phase disordered BCC solid solution without phase separation or secondary-phase formation.
